notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0006] Money-moving functions take idempotency_key: Every function that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance (e.g. refund in ledgerly/adjustments.py) must accept keyword-only idempotency_key=None, check ledgerly.audit.events() for an existing entry with that key first and return the original record without reapplying, and include idempotency_key in the audit.record call.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source INC-204; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
  WARNING: learned on version 1.0.0, this checkout is 2.0.0. Check CHANGELOG.md before relying on it.
- [at-0009] Record audit entry for every balance change: Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must call ledgerly.audit.record("<past_tense_event>", <entity>_id=..., amount=...) with payment_id=... or invoice_id=...; finance reconciles the ledger from these entries.
  (learned from task E06 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
  WARNING: learned on version 1.0.0, this checkout is 2.0.0. Check CHANGELOG.md before relying on it.
- [at-0010] Credits above threshold need second approver: Finance policy FIN-2026-09 requires a second approver for support-initiated refunds/credits above the approval threshold; enforce it by raising BillingError("approval_required") when the amount exceeds the threshold and no approver is supplied.
  (learned from task S04 on ledgerly 2.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Reject invalid input by raising `BillingError` from `ledgerly.errors` with a snake_case code such as `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity`, `negative_amount` or `invalid_amount`, and pass the offending value as the message.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 6x, 4 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0008] Normalize money and timestamps at entry: Normalize inputs at the top of money-handling functions: use ledgerly.money.round_money and ZERO for amounts and ledgerly.clock.ensure_utc for timestamps, and raise ledgerly.errors.BillingError with a snake_case code for validation failures.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 3x, 2 passed, 1 failed)

texts.at-0004: Exclude bool when validating integers When validating an integer argument, explicitly reject `bool` first (`isinstance(quantity, bool)`) because `True`/`False` pass `isinstance(x, int)` in Python.

review_comments: [team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above the approval threshold need a second approver: accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None` (callers that do not need approval keep working). Amounts at or below the threshold need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when `approved_by` is missing. The threshold is set by finance policy: 500.00 before 2.0.0, 1000.00 since 2.0.0 (see CHANGELOG).

candidate.title: Refund approval threshold is 1000.00 in 2.0.0
candidate.content: Support-initiated refunds/credits above the finance approval threshold require a second approver; since 2.0.0 (policy FIN-2026-09) the threshold is 1000.00 (it was 500.00 before). Expose it as a module-level constant in ledgerly/adjustments.py and raise BillingError("approval_required") when the amount exceeds it and no approver is supplied.

candidate.title: Round all money with round_money
candidate.content: Never round monetary values manually; use ledgerly.money.round_money (banker's rounding per FIN-2026-07) and compare against ledgerly.money.ZERO. Round incoming amounts and stored payment fields before arithmetic.
candidate.evidence_quote: `round_money()` now rounds half to even. Any code that rounds money on its own must be updated.
